title: Tension Trail
interaction_invariant: Click to anchor, drag to stretch a rainbow spring, release to launch the unicorn along its arc. Stretch length equals launch power but adds to a visible storm meter that drifts the next platforms, bends later springs, and dims past trails you may rebound off. Short risky springs keep the world calm; mastery is reading trajectory ghosts and rebounding off your own old trails.
player_goal: Chase the high-score distance ladder across an endless gap sequence before one missed landing ends the run.
controls: Mouse: press to anchor, drag to stretch and aim, release to launch; R instant restarts.
core_loop: Read the platform gap and your live storm meter.
Stretch and release a spring-leap, using old trails as rebounds.
Take stored tension as the next platforms drift and deform.
Land, chain, or miss and restart in one click.
prototype_scope: One arena and one complete playable run; prove the core interaction before breadth.
At most one enemy/boss archetype plus one escalation rule in this slice.
First meaningful player agency within 3 seconds after start/input unlock.
Target a 30-60 second representative run with immediate restart.
Do not implement meta progression, multiple levels, daily challenges, or category expansions.

state_machine.restart: dead/won -> fresh playing state with score, timers, entities, and input state reset

timing_contract.simulation: fixed-step 60 Hz accumulator or rigorously delta-time-scaled variable step

sensory_contract.visual: Procedural canvas: hue-cycled spring trails with fading trails, particle storm clouds scaled to the tension meter.
sensory_contract.audio: WebAudio: spring pitch and pluck timbre from stretch length, storm adds filtered noise layer, landing chimes arpeggiate with combo.
sensory_contract.readability: Core mechanic state, danger, success, and failure must be visible without reading debug text.

byte_priorities: polish only after the above survive browser/play evidence
non_goals: remote networking, fetch/post persistence, matchmaking, or leaderboards
requiring another human player; use a deterministic local echo/AI if a partner is intrinsic
touch-specific UI beyond basic pointer compatibility
more than one enemy/boss archetype in the first prototype
